name: spreader-bar
title: Spreader Bar
description: A customer logo wall hung as a Calder-style mobile: each mark's measured ink coverage sets where it hangs on its arm, and seven torsional pendulums at incommensurate periods keep the whole tree turning with no rest state.
instruction: Build <SpreaderBar logos? heading? className?> as a Canvas 2D logo wall rendered as a hanging mobile: 4 levels, 7 arms, 8 marks. WEIGHT: at mount (and whenever `logos` changes) rasterise each mark once onto an offscreen canvas, sum its alpha channel, and normalise to the set's mean — that normalised sum is the mark's weight `w`. BALANCE, the whole point of the component: build the tree bottom-up as nested arm nodes (root -> 2 level-2 arms -> 4 level-3 arms -> 8 leaf marks, 2 children per arm) and sum each subtree's weight recursively. For every arm, given its span S (the fixed distance between its two tips) and children weights wL/wR, solve d_left = S*wR/(wL+wR), d_right = S-d_left, clamped to [0.18, 0.82] of S so the fulcrum never touches a tip. The fulcrum (wire attachment, and the arm's rotation pivot) sits at that offset, not the arm's geometric centre — a heavier mark's subtree therefore hangs closer to its own fulcrum, and that asymmetry is the whole equalisation, never a hard-coded position. LAYOUT: level gap = max(34px, 0.19*min(w,h)) is the spec's own number; the arm taper (0.55x span per level) and root span (0.82*containerWidth) are builder-chosen to keep the 4-level tree non-overlapping at the extreme 0.18/0.82 d-clamp cases — the spec constrains only level height and the d-clamp fractions, not arm spans, so treat these two as tunable, not contractual. Base positions (fulcrums, hanger endpoints, mark centres) are computed once per resize/logos-change and are otherwise static. ROTATION IS TORSIONAL, NOT A SWING: every hanger wire is a torsional spring, so 'rotation' here means each arm and mark yaws about its own vertical wire — visible only as cos(theta) foreshortening of its drawn width, never as a position change ('nothing translates' is literal: base positions never move, only widths and a small luminance shade do). This reading is forced by the spec's own numbers, not a stylistic choice: the legibility floor is stated as a 34° cap so no mark drops below 0.83 of its frontal width, and cos(34deg) = 0.829 — that ratio is only meaningful under foreshortening about a vertical axis. Under an in-plane swing, frontal width would never change and the 0.83 floor would be an empty constraint; yaw is the only reading that makes 'nothing translates' and the 34° legibility cap true simultaneously. Seven arms carry deliberately incommensurate periods in seconds — root 26.8, level-2 17.2 and 21.5, level-3 7.3/9.1/11.6/13.9 — all at +-16 degrees amplitude; eight leaf marks spin at their own periods spread 5.9-8.7s at +-34 degrees amplitude, which is also the hard legibility cap (cos 34deg = 0.83, so no mark ever drops below 83% of its frontal width — clamp this in code, it is not a taste call). COUPLING: a child's instantaneous angle (normalised to its own amplitude) modulates its parent's effective period by +-4%, resolved bottom-up (leaves' uncoupled 'own spin' feeds level-3 arms, level-3 feeds level-2, level-2 feeds root) so the tree never reads as independent sine waves; a second top-down pass then gives each leaf its final angle, its own-spin period further modulated +-4% by its already-resolved parent arm ('inherit'). DRAUGHT: every arm and mark also gets an additive torque from a deterministic 1D value-noise field at 0.037Hz (a hash-based smooth noise, never Math.random, so the whole simulation stays a pure function of clock time), scaled to +-0.6% of that node's peak amplitude every frame — this, not the light air damping (Q=180, amplitude decaying with tau~400s), is why the mobile never settles: unforced, unbounded, no rest state and no cycle length. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE — do not reach for a spring integrator here: 'torsional pendulum, Q=180' reads like it wants an accumulating rAF ODE integration, but every angle in this component is instead a closed-form, stateless function of clock time t (decaying cosine, period modulated by coupling, plus the draught term). That is deliberate: prefers-reduced-motion and the pause button both freeze by evaluating that same function once at STATIC_TIME, and only a pure function of t makes that freeze frame byte-stable on every load — an accumulating integrator would make byte-stability a matter of float drift and frame timing luck, which fails the reduced-motion gate. Keep the pure-function structure on any future edit. SHADING: a fixed overhead light gives each mark +-0.06 L by mixing --foreground toward literal white (lightening) or black (darkening) in proportion to sin(theta) — hangers and arms are not shaded. TOKENS: --foreground (marks @0.82 alpha, pivot dots @0.55) and --ns-muted (arms @0.70, hangers @0.50) only, read via getComputedStyle at mount and re-read on a MutationObserver watching documentElement's class, before any draw call — --border and --ns-accent never appear in the canvas; --ns-accent shows only on the pause button's focus ring. RENDER: Canvas 2D, DPR-capped backing store at 2, ResizeObserver on the host re-solves the whole layout, IntersectionObserver-offscreen and visibilitychange both halt the single rAF loop. prefers-reduced-motion and the 'Pause motion' button both freeze on the same deterministic function evaluated once at t=14.6s (STATIC_TIME) — byte-stable regardless of how long the page has been open, because nothing in the simulation accumulates state across frames. ACCESSIBILITY: the canvas is aria-hidden; the real content is a DOM <ul> of company names/links under the mobile in document order, and a single <button aria-pressed> 'Pause motion' is the only tab stop the canvas contributes — no aria-live, since nothing here is a value.
useWhen: Pick spreader-bar when the logo set has visibly unequal marks (a wordmark next to a monogram, a heavy glyph next to a hairline one) and you want the wall to prove it handles that rather than hide it. Pick logo-cloud-settle instead for an even, entrance-only grid where every tile carries the same weight; pricing-scale instead when you need a two-sided argument (exactly two things being weighed), not a tree of many.
